instantiated_cells.justification: The only periodic spending/expense statement in the provided text is the principal's expense statement due July 31 and January 31; no annual lobbyist-filed spending report is specified.
Section 13.68 requires semiannual filing by principals, not monthly lobbyist spending reports.
The statute assigns the periodic expense statement filing duty to principals and only requires lobbyists to provide information to principals, not to file separate reports on another cadence.
Expense statements are required semiannually from principals (July 31/Jan 31), not quarterly from lobbyists.
The statute requires 'Every principal' registered under §13.64 to file the semiannual expense statement; it does not require lobbyists to file a separate semiannual spending report.
No triannual/legislative-calendar spending report filed by lobbyists is described; only the principal's semiannual expense statement is required.
Itemization requirements in §13.68 apply to the principal's expense statement, while the lobbyist only provides supporting information to the principal rather than filing a separate itemized report.

The statute requires principals to file expense statements and directs lobbyists to furnish information for those statements, but imposes no separate periodic spending report filing requirement on lobbyists.
Section 13.67 requires the principal to report legislative proposals/rules/topics to the board, not the lobbyist as the filer of a separate spending/activity report.
Compensation to lobbyists is reported by the principal in its expense statement, but the statute does not mandate a lobbyist-filed disclosure of amounts received from clients.
The principal's expense statement requires time records and certain disclosures, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a contacts disclosure report.
Time-spent proportions by proposal/topic are required in the principal's expense statement, not an expenditure-per-issue disclosure by a lobbyist in a separate report.
Issue/topic identification is a principal reporting obligation under §13.67(1), not a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requirement.
General subjects/topics of lobbying are reported by principals to the board under §13.67(1), not by lobbyists as separate filers.

Although gifts/food/transportation are generally prohibited under §13.625 and principals report certain reimbursed expenses under §13.68, the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report component for such costs.
Indirect lobbying costs are disclosed through the principal's expense statement, with lobbyists only supplying supporting information rather than filing their own report.
Wisconsin requires principals (not lobbyists) to file the periodic expense statement, so lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports including issues/bills and compensation.

The lobbyist license application requires a social security number and is filed with the board, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report disclosing their address/phone number.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/rules/topics is a principal's reporting duty under §13.67(1), not a lobbyist-filed activity/spending report requirement.
Nature of business is disclosed on the principal's registration statement under §13.64, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.

The principal registration statement includes the principal's name and business address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report disclosing principals' addresses/phone numbers.

Authorizations to represent a principal are filed by the lobbyist or principal under §13.65, but there is no requirement that lobbyists file a separate periodic spending report listing all principals represented.
Reporting of legislative proposal numbers and proposed administrative rule numbers is assigned to principals under §13.67(1), not to lobbyists via a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are reported by principals in the principal expense statement, not by lobbyists as separate periodic filers.

Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal's aggregate totals under §13.68(1)(a), while lobbyists only provide information to principals under §13.68(4) and do not file their own totals.
Because the periodic itemized expense statement is filed by principals and lobbyists merely supply information, the statute does not require lobbyists to file the described itemized spending reports.
The statute imposes no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report at all, so it does not require lobbyists to file 'no activity' reports.

Section 13.625(6) provides a household/relative exception to gift restrictions but the reporting regime in the provided text does not impose a lobbyist spending report that would require reporting spending on household members of officials.
Itemized disclosures exist within the principal's expense statement (filed by the principal), but there is no separate lobbyist-filed itemized spending report under the statute.
